transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Emily Banks (CFO, Veridian Assurance), Marco Ruiz (Lead Cloud Engineer, Veridian), Dr. Asha Nair (Head of Security, Veridian)
---
Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Customer is evaluating Redwood for a mixture of hosted and dedicated inference for financial workflows. Primary blockers are customer-managed keys, key escrow policy for long-term archival, and strict EU residency for PII and audit logs. They requested SOC2/ISO evidence and an architectural diagram showing where keys live and how logs are redacted before leaving their environment.
---
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh Samir from Redwood here. appreciate you carving time. quick roll call?
[00:10] Emily: Emily here, hi.
[00:12] Marco: Marco, cloud.
[00:14] Asha: Asha here.
[00:16] Lena: Lena from SE, hi all.
[00:18] Samir: cool. objective for today is to map key residency and escrow needs, and figure out whether Hosted + Dedicated is viable or we need a Private deployment, right?
[00:28] Emily: exactly. procurement timeline is tight, end of Q2 ideally. we need to decide which hosting mode meets our audit controls.
[00:36] Marco: and technical constraints — latencies, throughput, plus where the keys live, who can access, and what the audit trail looks like.
[00:44] Asha: for us the big ones are GDPR egress, customer-managed keys (BYOK), and an independent escrow policy for legal hold. also want to avoid sending raw PII into a multi-tenant service logs.
[00:55] Samir: totally. let's start with keys. we support BYOK via KMS integrations; you can bring keys from cloud KMS (Google KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) or use an HSM-backed flow. Lena, want to give the quick folksy architecture?
[01:12] Lena: yeah. at a high level, for Hosted we offer a customer-managed key mode where the encryption keys are stored in your KMS and we request short-lived wrapping keys when needed. the model weights and artifacts are encrypted at rest with keys that are either rooted to your KMS or to Redwood-managed keys depending on the option. for Dedicated you can choose dedicated tenancy with network isolation and still keep keys in your KMS. for Private you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem and you keep all keys locally — nothing leaves your environment.
[01:46] Marco: when you say "request short-lived wrapping keys" — are we pushing key material to Redwood? we need explicit no-export guarantees for key material.
[01:55] Lena: good question. we do NOT accept raw private key material. we only accept wrapped keys or a KMS policy that issues short-lived data encryption keys (DEKs) to the Redwood runtime. the unwrapped key material never leaves your KMS. i will add that our HSM partners can support dual-control signatures if you need escrow operations to be two-person authorized.
[02:18] Asha: hmm dual control is good. second: we have an internal legal requirement to escrow keys for 7+ years for archived records. how does that map to BYOK and HSM?
[02:30] Samir: key escrow for long-term archival is not standard for cloud KMS, but there are approaches: one is a third-party escrow provider that holds an encrypted copy under dual-control; another is to use an on-prem HSM appliance as the root and have backups replicated to an escrow partner. we can document the pattern and provide checklist language for your auditors.
[02:50] Emily: that's promising, but we need an example architecture for auditors showing who has access and how the escrow lifecycle works.
[02:58] Lena: we can produce that. i'll include both Hosted + Dedicated diagrams: Hosted with KMS in eu-west-1, Redwood runtime in dedicated GPU pool also in eu-west-1, logs routed to your SIEM via VPC peering and a redaction hook before export. Dedicated still means Redwood controls the runtime but you control network boundaries and keys.
[03:22] Marco: do you have an example of the log redaction hook? we prefer to sanitize logs in our sidecar before they hit Redwood's logging system — any support for that?
[03:33] Lena: yes — we have a pre-ingest hook customers use. the flow: model request hits your VPC ingress, your sidecar does PII tokenization/redaction, you forward sanitized request to Redwood endpoint. for Hosted we provide an SDK that supports client-side redaction as well. for Private, all logs stay local unless you explicitly forward them.
[03:55] Asha: ok, and about audit logs -- we need immutable audit trails capturing token-level access for 3 years. retention and region-locking are critical. does Redwood support region-locked audit retention?
[04:08] Samir: yes we support region-locking for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be region-scoped but might have control plane metadata that is global; we can show the exact data flows. retention windows are configurable; for EU residency you can set data to stay in eu-west-1 and we can configure not to replicate to a secondary region.
[04:26] Emily: any limitations for streaming / real-time inference? we do low-latency trading-ops inference in EU and can't have additional egress latencies.
[04:35] Lena: Dedicated pools in-region, colocated with GPU hosts, have predictable latencies. Private on-prem has the lowest network hops but higher ops overhead. Hosted may add small control-plane hops but data path can be in-region; we'll provide benchmark numbers for median p95 latency for similar customers.
[04:55] Marco: curious about bursting — say we need sudden scale; if keys are in our KMS and you need to request DEKs frequently, does that affect rate-limits?
[05:06] Samir: we design for that; we'll show recommended KMS quota settings. for extreme bursty loads we can advise local caching of wrapped DEKs for a short TTL while preserving compliance controls. caching TTL is a policy knob.
[05:20] Asha: ok. next question: encryption at rest for model artifacts and commit logs — you mentioned either Redwood-rooted or customer-rooted keys. if we pick customer-rooted, what parts still rely on Redwood-managed keys?
[05:34] Lena: with customer-rooted keys, persistent storage — model blobs, checkpoints — are wrapped with DEKs derived from your CMK; Redwood-managed keys are not required. ephemeral runtime caches may use short-lived keys that are wrapped by your KMS. we can make that fully auditable with key IDs logged.
[05:50] Emily: regulatory team also asked about legal process: if a subpoena arrives in a non-EU jurisdiction can Redwood be compelled to hand keys or logs?
[06:01] Samir: great question. if keys are customer-managed in your KMS, Redwood cannot unilaterally decrypt without a key release — so control sits with you. for Hosted where keys are Redwood-managed, legal process could come into play. Private keeps everything under your control. we'll include legal language examples for the contract.
[06:20] Marco: can you show an example contract clause for cross-border log transfers or for a legal hold that we can feed to our counsel?
[06:27] Samir: yes we'll provide sample contract snippets and a compliance matrix that maps feature to contract clause.
[06:33] Asha: on logging — we need to ensure PII never leaves EU, but we also want Redwood to provide telemetry for SLOs (token counts, latencies). can you provide aggregated telemetry without raw content?
[06:47] Lena: absolutely. we can emit telemetry that is token-level metrics (counts/timings) and error traces while keeping request/response bodies redacted. that's part of our Optimize toolkit — cost/latency diagnostics can be surfaced without raw payloads.
[07:01] Emily: good. another blocker: SOC2 attestation and penetration test results. we need SOC2 Type II and a summary of pentest scope.
[07:10] Samir: we have SOC2 Type II report and some penetration test attestations; we share them under an NDA. we'll push the SOC2 report and the third-party pentest summary in the packet.
[07:20] Marco: any certifications for HSM providers? our security team requires FIPS 140-2 validated modules for escrow workflows.
[07:28] Lena: our HSM partners are FIPS-validated; we'll flag the module and firmware versions in the doc.
[07:34] Asha: retention policies for logs — our legal asks for a conditional redaction process: maintain full audit trail but redact PII fields from logs after 30 days unless there's an ongoing investigation. can Redwood support rule-based redaction with tombstoning?
[07:51] Lena: yes. we support rule-based redaction and tombstone markers. we can also support an encrypted archive where raw logs go to your escrow HSM with controlled access in case of investigation.
[08:04] Emily: sounds like there are a lot of options. procurement will want one recommended path. what do you typically recommend for financial services folks with residency + escrow needs?
[08:15] Samir: most FS customers choose Dedicated with BYOK in their cloud KMS in-region (eu-west-1), plus a third-party key escrow for long-term archives. if they want full control and zero control-plane exposure they choose Private. Dedicated is often a good middle ground: lower ops lift, still strong isolation and region-locking.
[08:32] Marco: any differences in logging scope between Dedicated and Private?
[08:36] Lena: Private gives you complete control — logs never leave your network unless you configure export. Dedicated gives strong boundaries and region locks but some control-plane metadata (billing/usage) may be outside the region; we can document exactly which telemetry flows where.
[08:53] Asha: ok, procurement question — do you support vendor escrow for keys in case Redwood is acquired or shuts down? our counsel insists on vendor continuity plans.
[09:02] Samir: yes we have continuity options: contractual vendor escrow, data export playbooks, and a transfer plan for keys. with BYOK, the critical part is that the root is yours; with Redwood-managed keys we'd offer a documented export path plus an escrow deposit. we'll include an example SLA attachment.
[09:20] Marco: curious on motion for private deployment — how long to stand up a private control plane on-prem?
[09:27] Lena: a typical on-prem Private deployment setup is 6–10 weeks for a standard rack + network tuning, shorter if you already have a validated image or if you go with our appliance. Dedicated provisioning can be done faster — maybe 2–3 weeks for reserved GPU pools in a cloud region.
[09:45] Emily: budget question — is Dedicated significantly more expensive than Hosted?
[09:50] Samir: Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing (committed), so unit costs may be lower at scale but you'll have a fixed commit. Hosted is pay-as-you-go; sometimes cheaper for low/variable volume. Private adds a platform fee plus ops. we'll include a cost comparison spreadsheet.
[10:04] Marco: ok. technical deep dive request: we'd like to test a small pipeline with our model and KMS in eu-west-1 and see key-wrapping behavior and log redaction. can Redwood run a POC with a dedicated pool and our keys?
[10:18] Samir: yes — we can run a 30–60 day POC with a small dedicated pool or a Private eval. typical approach: start with a Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 with your CMK and run sample requests and we capture telemetry and key usage logs for audit.
[10:33] Asha: what data do you need from us to scope the POC?
[10:36] Lena: sample request volumes, model size, and a compliance checklist (what fields are PII). Marco you said you'll send the checklist. also need an NDA to share SOC2.
[10:47] Marco: yes i'll send checklist and escrow vendor preferences.
[10:50] Samir: perfect. on the legal side we'll redline an amendment referencing key custody, escrow, export rights, and region-binding.
[10:59] Emily: an odd question — what about backups? if you do backups of model state, are they encrypted with the same keys and do they support separate retention?
[11:08] Lena: backups/incremental checkpoints are encrypted with the same DEK strategy; retention and separate lifecycle policies are supported — you can set different TTLs and whether they are exported to archived storage (and escrowed). we'll include a backup lifecycle example.
[11:26] Marco: small nit — you mentioned earlier that control-plane metadata might be global for Hosted. do you have a data flow diagram showing what metadata exists outside the region?
[11:34] Samir: yes we'll include a control-plane/data-plane diagram. typically usage metrics and billing metadata may be aggregated for UX but we can provide region-bound alternatives in an enterprise SLA.
[11:43] Asha: will you also include a matrix of who can access keys and under what conditions? for us the separation of duties is critical.
[11:50] Lena: yes — we'll show an RBAC matrix and examples of HSM dual-control for escrow retrieval, and operational procedures.
[11:58] Emily: timeline wise — procurement needs a recommended path and sample contract language by next week. is that doable?
[12:05] Samir: we can get a package out by Friday. that'll include SOC2 (NDA), KMS architecture diagrams, recommended Dedicated configuration for eu-west-1, cost comparison, and sample contract snippets.
[12:17] Marco: you mentioned redaction hooks. can we see a small code sample of the SDK call flow and how to run redaction in the sidecar?
[12:25] Lena: yes, i'll include a short code snippet and a runnable container example for the POC.
[12:30] Asha: one last compliance question — for HIPAA overlap (we have some healthcare-adjacent accounts), do you have any reference for how Redwood's retention and BAAs line up?
[12:40] Samir: we do sign BAAs for Private and Dedicated enterprise agreements; Hosted BAAs are evaluated case-by-case. we'll include BAA terms and HIPAA mapping in the packet.
[12:51] Emily: thanks. sounds good.
[12:54] Samir: thanks all. quick recap of next steps: we'll send a POC proposal for a dedicated pool in eu-west-1, include KMS architecture and escrow options, provide SOC2/pentest under NDA, deliver a redaction hook example, and propose the technical deep dive next Tue (2027-05-11).
[13:10] Marco: confirmed i'll send the checklist by Friday.
[13:14] Asha: and we'll review the SOC2 under NDA.
[13:18] Lena: we'll get the doc pack out by Friday.
[13:22] Samir: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the CRM and set the deep dive invite.
